title: Little decisions and defining moments
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Which small decision has been quietly shaping your life?

Jose explained two ideas: gradualism, a steady slow change, and punctualism, short bursts of change with periods of stability between them. A student said: there are thousands of experiences an hour but probably ten or twenty defining moments that make you who you are, so it leans toward punctualism.
Jose said that awareness of your habits leads to a higher frequency of the moments that define the rest of your life.

Jose said that you can think for a long time, but the moment you decide and act is a matter of seconds. A student said: if you take more time, then that was not the decision moment because you were not committed yet; the moment of commitment is only an instant.
Jose said that in failure it is a lot of little decisions that accumulate, not one decision. He said it is all process in the end.
A student gave a negative example of one small choice repeated until it becomes a routine, and then a problem. It started with a single decision. The details are left out.

Jose said that your thought habits and physical habits create the fertile ground for the significant moments, such as a move to a place you believe in. If you are not in control of them, or are in a destructive environment, you do not have that ground.

A student said: do it now; enjoy the significant life you are creating today. Jose added the saying that it is not the act but the accompanying consciousness, whose source he could not recall and is to be verified.
What decision are you putting off, and what small decisions lead to it?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a defining moment in your life.
Write the little decisions that led to it.
Write a decision you are putting off.
Write the small decisions that lead to it.
Write the consciousness you want with each act.

check.q: What did Jose say failure is made of?
What did a student say about the decision moment?
What did Jose say creates the fertile ground for significant moments?

recap: Little decisions add up. The decision is an instant. Prepare the ground.
